holidays.name: National Hug a Drummer Day
holidays.description: Give some love to the person keeping the whole band in time. Drummers spend their gigs hidden at the back, hauling heavy gear and getting very little attention. Today is the day to thank them with a hug, or at least a fist bump and a round of applause.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, fun observance. Its creator is unclear, but it has become a favorite among musicians and music lovers.
holidays.funFact: A drummer's workout is real exercise. Playing a long set can burn as many calories as a brisk session of cardio, which makes the hug well earned.

holidays.name: National Cake Decorating Day
holidays.description: A day for piping, swirling, sprinkling and frosting. Bakers of every skill level are encouraged to turn a plain cake into an edible work of art, whether it ends up elegant or hilariously lopsided.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the baking craft of turning simple cakes into showpieces.
holidays.funFact: Modern piped-icing cake decoration took off in the 19th century. Its popularity grew once cooks had pastry bags and metal piping tips to work with.

holidays.name: National Handbag Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble carryall, which holds keys, snacks, emergency supplies and sometimes a whole life. Show off your favorite bag, clean out the mystery items at the bottom, or treat yourself to a new one.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the bag as both a fashion statement and a practical tool.
holidays.funFact: Handbags have a long history. People once wore pouches tied at the waist, and the modern purse grew out of those pouches centuries ago.
